description: Derived nodes on live data: Tempo's service graph is edges-only, so every node in these panels is one the response never declared. converters/deriveNodes.ts declares them as fields above the panel so field overrides can reach them — which requires the panel-registered transformations API (grafana/grafana#129992). This stack's Grafana does NOT have it yet, so this dashboard is the before half of the before/after: the graphs draw correctly, and every per-node override is inert except hiding, which the panel still re-reads by name. Kept live so it flips on its own the day the API lands. The TestData version of the same proof is ECharts Relations — derived nodes, mounted into this stack from the repo's own provisioning.
title: ECharts Relations — derived nodes on live service-graph data (LGTM)

options.content:
# Derived nodes, on data nobody shaped for the panel

`traces_service_graph_request_total{client, server}` describes **edges**. It says `user` called `grafana`, and `prometheus` scraped itself; it never says what a `grafana` *is*. Neither does any other service-graph metric, in this stack or in Grafana Cloud — the node set is whatever the endpoints add up to.

The panel has always drawn those nodes. What it could not do is let you **configure** one, because a node invented inside the panel arrives after `applyFieldOverrides` has run, and a mark with no field is a mark Grafana's config pipeline cannot address: no colour, no radius, no subtitle, no data link, no hide. `converters/deriveNodes.ts` fixes that by declaring each implied endpoint as an ordinary field of a `graph-nodes-wide` frame, in the pipeline prefix the plugin registers on itself — **above** the panel, before the override pass.

## This dashboard is currently the *before* picture

The prefix runs through `PanelPlugin.setDataTransformations` ([grafana/grafana#129992](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/129992)), gated behind `grafana.panelPluginTransformations`. Neither exists in this stack's Grafana, so on **this** host:

- the graphs below draw, correctly and completely — the reader still derives the nodes itself;
- colour, radius, `displayName`, subtitle and data links on panel 3 are **silently inert**;
- **hiding still works.** `hiddenNodeIds` falls back to matching a fieldless node by *name*, which is the one by-name read the family kept and kept for exactly this case — so `grafana-assistant-app` is missing from panel 3 even here;
- nothing errors, and nothing is missing that was ever there.

When the API lands, the rest start landing too, with no dashboard change. Until then the honest comparison is panel 2 against panel 3: on this host they differ by one hidden node and nothing else; on a host with the flag they differ by all three overrides.

The same proof against TestData, where it can be run today, is in **ECharts Relations — derived nodes** (mounted into this stack from the repo's `provisioning/dashboards/relations`). Background: `docs/relations-derived-nodes.md`.

panels.title: Control — the live service graph, nothing configured
panels.description:
Every node here — `user`, `grafana`, `prometheus`, `alloy`, `grafana-assistant-app` — is derived. The query groups by `source` and `target` and returns one ranged series per edge; no frame in the response names a node.

`prometheus → prometheus` is Prometheus scraping itself, a genuine self-loop. `user` is Tempo's own virtual node for requests that arrived with no client span — unrelated to a derived node, and a good reminder that the two words mean different things here.

panels.title: The same graph, with three overrides on nodes nothing declared
panels.description:
**Identical query and options to the control.** The only difference is `fieldConfig.overrides`, naming three services that appear in no frame Prometheus returned:

- **`grafana`** → dark red, radius 34, renamed **Grafana (this stack)**
- **`user`** → a `Subtitle` row and a data link into the Tempo docs, both tooltip-only
- **`grafana-assistant-app`** → `custom.hideFrom.viz`, so the node and the edge into it are gone

**On this host only the third one takes effect.** The nodes are invented inside the panel, downstream of the override engine, so `byName` has nothing to match for colour, radius, `displayName`, subtitle or links — but hiding is re-read by name in the panel (`hiddenNodeIds`), so `grafana-assistant-app` really is gone. Compare with the control: one node's difference, where there should be three overrides' worth.

On a Grafana with `grafana.panelPluginTransformations` the pre-pass declares each node as a field first and all three land. Verified in that state against a source-built 13.2 (`docs/relations-derived-nodes.md`); the equivalent TestData panel is panel 2 of **ECharts Relations — derived nodes**.

panels.title: Show node values — a derived node has no stat to show
panels.description:
"Show node values" is on and every label is still a single line. There is nothing to reduce: the field the pre-pass creates for an implied node holds `null`, and on this host the node has no field at all.

It used to print the node's **degree** here — a count of the links naming it, sitting in the slot a request rate goes in, formatted with whichever unit the first edge happened to carry. On a service graph that read as a per-service measurement and was not one.

The edges keep their real stat: hover any line and the tooltip reads `req/s` off that edge's own field.
